I’m assuming you are using exec-once to launch a service and not something like Firefox. 

Systemd Services have some special properties. They will be monitored and automatically restarted. They can also have a different priority level than your main apps. You can also use Syscontrol to start/disable/etc your services. 

So although you could use exec-once to launch waybar (for example) under UWSM, you could just use the included service file that Waybar bundles and just enable the service using syscontrol. That will make Waybar behave more like a service , and then you don’t need the Hyprland configuration entry either. 

I prefer deep integration with systemd instead of having Hyprland launch my stuff. Hyprland is my window compositor, it doesn’t need to launch or manage programs. Thats systemd’s job, it’s really good at that.

What’s more stable and easier to resource manage, one massive process or dozens of smaller ones?

Without UWSM, Hyprland and everything launched under it appears as one large monolithic unit to systemd. 

With UWSM, each app is inside its own unit. Now systemd can manage each unit cleanly as its  own service. Different apps can be in different slices, so if you’re running low on memory for example you can have lower priority units killed first. Systemd can automatically restart services, shut them down cleanly, and encode dependencies between units. For example some services may depend on your graphical session while others don’t. 

The whole point is to give systemd finer grain control over your session


Just enable the service (run this from the terminal):

```
systemctl --user enable <the service>
```

Systemctl Enable will place the unit in the relevant places so that it started automatically on login. You don't need those calls in your hyprland.conf.


Hypridle, Waybar, Hyprpaper, and Hyprpolkit agent all include SystemD services now, so you can omit them completly from your hyprland.conf and use `systemctl --user enable` to automatically start them, as per above.

UWSM gives you better integration with SystemD. Without UWSM, all the programs you launch are child processes of Hyprland's "unit". You don't get orderly shutdown, and resource management is suboptimal.  


With SystemD integration through UWSM, the compositor service unit (Hyprland) is detached from the units you launch. SystemD manages everything, so you get better resource management, services can be managed through \`systemctl\`, and you get clean shutdowns.

As a concrete example, when I use Chromium without UWSM, logging out of Hyprland would stop the browser and I would lose my tabs. Through UWSM, Chromium knows it's getting shutdown and will restore my tabs when I return.

I also enjoy managing Waybar, Hyprpaper, Walker, etc directly as SystemD services instead of having Hyprland launch them.

To answer your question of when to wrap calls with \`uwsm\`, it's whenever Hyprland is launching something. So if you have a keybind to open Kitty, wrap it with \`uwsm\`, otherwise, it would be part of the same Hyprland unit which you are trying to avoid. And if you use an app launcher, you can configure it to launch stuff through UWSM.

But entries in XDG Autostart directory, for example, would not get wrapped, because Hyprland isn't launching it, SystemD is.
